title: Dashboard "stop chain" does not stop buying: HTTP-polling chains keep polling and buying, Telegram alpha drops still route to stopped chains, and "start" adds a second poller

evidence.note: stop route: adds the chain to stoppedChains and calls ctx.wsProvider.removeAllListeners() only when a WS provider exists
only src/api/routes/chains.ts and src/api/server.ts reference stoppedChains: no buy handler and no Telegram routing consults it
chains without a WS URL use startHttpPollingListener
the V2 poller is a setInterval whose handle is discarded: nothing can clear it, so stop has no effect on it
Telegram routing sends an address to every context whose chain has code there, stopped or not
onRestart calls startDexListener again; for an HTTP chain that starts a second poller, so every event is dispatched twice (feeds AUD-BUY-004)
codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Chain restart accumulates listeners and uncancellable polling intervals

sibling_sites_checked: Every buy entry point checked for a stop check: V2 WS listener, V3 WS listener, both HTTP pollers, Telegram -> alphaDrop -> both handlers, onRestart. None checks stoppedChains. The pause flag is checked at CP1/CP2 in both handlers (bot.ts:1034-1040, :1066-1072, :1351-1357, :1401-1407). The API slice owns chains.ts; it is read, not edited.
severity_rationale: S1: the operator control that reads "stopped" leaves capital being committed on a chain configured without a WebSocket URL, and for every Telegram-routed token on any chain. Plausible condition (operator uses stop; HTTP fallback or Telegram enabled). The global pause (CP1/CP2 checks in both handlers) is unaffected and does stop new buys, which keeps this at S1.
recommendation: Make "stopped" a state every buy entry point honours (handlers, pollers and Telegram routing), keep the poller handle so stop clears it and start cannot duplicate it, or remove the per-chain stop/start in favour of the global pause. Card BUY-04. Until fixed, use the global pause, not per-chain stop, to halt buying. Phase 24; nothing is changed in Phase 22.
